frontier.hypothesis: A C form exists that makes the class-C reload pseudo fail local-alloc.c:469-477 (reg_qty = -1) WITHOUT introducing a long-lived named local - which would keep g1's byte-exact rows 60-78 while leaving rows 79-89 (the 0x5C/0x60 block) untouched. That form scores 3 minus the class-C rows plus only the rows 38-59 loop-head cost, and if the loop head can be held, it is a score-0 body.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c:469-477 sets reg_qty = -1 when reg_basic_block < 0 OR reg_n_deaths != 1; g1 satisfied both at once (two sets AND uses straddling the inner loop). Only ONE is needed. g4 proves two reads inside a single basic block are refolded by cse and never materialise a second set, so the second death has to come from a read the cse table cannot merge - i.e. one separated from the first by a store or a call, which the inner loop's own stores already provide.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate spellings that give the reload exactly ONE of the two disqualifiers: (a) reg_n_deaths == 2 with both uses in the SAME block by placing the second read after the inner loop's first store but keeping the 0x5C/0x60 stores as anonymous global reads; (b) reg_basic_block == -1 with a single set, by reading the global into a local BEFORE the p_6a/p_7e block and using it once more in the immediately following block only. Read reg_n_deaths / reg_basic_block for the reload pseudo straight out of the .lreg dump for each build (tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s31/slice.py) rather than inferring from the score.

frontier.hypothesis: The rows 38-59 loop-head reschedule that BOTH class-C fixes pay is a separable sched1 decision, not a fixed price of the flipped tie.
frontier.mechanism: In f1 and g1 the loop-top `lw %gp_rel(D_800A36A0)` moves one slot earlier (ours row 40 vs target row 41) and the group-A pointer re-seats from $v0 to $a1, propagating through rows 42-59. sched.c's ready-list priority for the loop-top load changes once the downstream sum's quantity changes seat, so this is the same sched1/local-alloc coupling s28-s30 named on the flipped-cursor chassis - but now on the A-first chassis, where the rest of the window is already byte-exact.
frontier.next_probe: Take g1 as the base (rows 60-78 byte-exact) and vary ONLY the loop head: the position of `u8 *base = D_800A36A0;`, whether group A is addressed off `base` or off a re-read, and the statement order of the A/D/C/S groups. Diff the .sched dump's ready-list for the loop-top load between d1F and g1 to name which dependency edge changed.

frontier.next_probe: Audit the callers and the record layout at D_800A36A0 + 0x4 for a genuine list-walk shape in the surrounding functions (func_8006E49C, func_80076FF8, func_8006E950): if any of them establishes that this block is a push onto a linked list, the natural C for the push may reassign p_old on its own.
